text:
customer_acme_ops: Hey @support, our private VPC endpoints to Redwood started failing after we rotated our internal root CA overnight. Getting TLS failures from our services that call the Redwood Private control plane.

support_sam: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste the exact error you're seeing and a quick repro?

customer_acme_ops: Error from our side: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in the client logs. The control-plane logs show `tls: received certificate is not trusted` on some connections. This started after we rolled our corporate root (we swapped the root cert in our internal PKI and pushed new intermediates).

sre_jordan: Two quick questions: 1) Are you terminating TLS at your edge (LB) or passing through to Redwood Private instances? 2) Can you run `openssl s_client -connect <redwood-host>:443 -servername <redwood-host> -showcerts` from a host in the same VPC and paste output?

customer_acme_ops: We're terminating TLS at HAProxy edge and forwarding to Redwood with TLS passthrough. I ran the openssl command from a bastion and it returns only a single cert (the leaf) and no intermediate chain:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private-api.redwood.example
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=private-api.redwood.example
   i:/CN=SomeIntermediate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...leaf...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

support_sam: That's telling — your HAProxy may be stripping or not sending the full chain to clients. Also, if your edge replaced the root, maybe the intermediate bundle ordering changed and OCSP/CRL lookups fail if egress is blocked.

eng_maya: A couple of things to check: 1) HAProxy needs to serve `fullchain.pem` (leaf + intermediate(s)) as `crt` in the frontend. 2) If your clients do OCSP stapling validation or the control plane does client cert verification, ensure your egress allowlist permits access to OCSP responders and any CRL distribution points for the intermediates.

customer_acme_ops: We don't stapling on the edge, but our outbound firewall is very strict. What endpoints should we allow?

eng_maya: Common ones: the intermediate/issuer's OCSP URL(s) (look inside the cert `AuthorityInfoAccess`), and any public CA CRL URLs if used. If your intermediate is corporate, ensure your internal OCSP responder is reachable from the subnet doing TLS verification. Also check that HAProxy is not configured with `http-reuse` or `tcp-request` that rewrites TLS.

customer_acme_ops: I checked `AuthorityInfoAccess` — OCSP URL points to `ocsp.corp-pki.internal`. That host is blocked by our egress rules for the subnets where Redwood probes run. So likely OCSP lookup fails. But why would that cause chain verify errors if clients have the root?

sre_jordan: If the control plane or your client library validates revocation and can't reach OCSP, some libraries treat that as a hard failure depending on policy. Also if the server (or HAProxy) is sending only the leaf and the client does strict validation, the chain can't be built to a trusted root. The server must provide intermediates. We saw the `Certificate chain` above has only depth 0 which matches that.

support_sam: Quick repro step we usually ask: from your bastion run `curl -v --resolve private-api.redwood.example:443:<redwood-ip> https://private-api.redwood.example/health` and paste the TLS debug. That often surfaces missing chain vs hostname issues.

customer_acme_ops: Ran that, curl shows `SSL: certificate subjectAltName does not match` sometimes and other times `SSL: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Looks intermittent across pods.

eng_maya: Intermittent sounds like mixed config during rollout: some HAProxy instances might be serving old `fullchain` while others serve only leaf. Also if you rotated the intermediate ordering (cross-signed vs new intermediate) some clients will prefer different paths.

customer_acme_ops: Ugh — we did a rolling deploy of a new HAProxy config yesterday. Probably some hosts got the new cert file without the intermediate.

sre_jordan: Action plan: 1) Confirm every HAProxy has `crt` set to a fullchain file (leaf + all intermediates concatenated, correct order). 2) Ensure firewall allows egress to your OCSP responder from the subnets performing TLS verification (and from any Redwood side agents if you use mutual TLS). 3) On one affected host run `openssl s_client -connect <redwood-host>:443 -showcerts -status` to see OCSP stapling status. 4) Collect `haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg` and the cert files from two hosts (one good, one bad).

customer_acme_ops: I'll check configs and open a ticket with our network team to allow ocsp.corp-pki.internal from the VPC subnets. Sharing the `haproxy -c` output now.

support_sam: Thanks — if you want a temporary mitigation, we can enable a compatibility fallback on the control plane to accept the chain if it verifies via alternative path for 24 hours while you finish the rollout. Need eng approval. @eng_maya can you OK a short window?

eng_maya: We can enable a temporary relaxation on the control plane for client verification for a single customer for up to 6 hours while they fix edge config — low risk but needs auditing. Please confirm exactly when so we can schedule and log the change.

customer_acme_ops: ETA for full rollout fix is 2 hours. Please enable the temporary relaxation starting in ~30 minutes, for 3 hours. We'll push fullchain to all HAProxy hosts in that window.

sre_jordan: Noted. Also request a tcpdump from one failing host: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/tls-dump.pcap host <redwood-ip> and port 443` while repro happens — will help us confirm what certs are exchanged.

ops-bot: INC-2026 created for "ACME private TLS failures during root rotation" assigned to support_sam, priority P2.

support_sam: Got the pcap and haproxy outputs — confirmed mismatch. I'll coordinate the relaxation window and follow up once eng flips the flag. Thanks all for the quick diagnostics. :thumbsup:

customer_acme_ops: Thanks everyone, pushing fixes now. Will post back when done.
